Without it, 'no failures' would read identically for 'they all passed' and 'none of them ran' - the same shape as the fetch stage, where 'nothing changed' would have read identically for 'the fetch ran and brought zero' and 'the fetch never ran'. It is a gate (exit 11), not a note, and it was drilled: a stubbed instrument leaving sixteen at not_run produced exit 11 naming all sixteen.
streams.what_the_number_is_and_is_NOT: A LOWER bound on the hook's duration, and the coordinator's caveat is carried as mine: the page cache is warm here and this checkout is not fresh, while the hook creates its tree a moment before use. It will also be the first measurement of this 19-command route that anyone has: nobody has ever timed it, and bin/skipi-guard contains no perf_counter, time.time, monotonic, elapsed, duration or datetime.now, so the skipi-guard.v1 JSON cannot carry timing BY CONSTRUCTION and every duration must come from an external bracket.

The FORM matches and not merely the content - which is the lesson from stage 5, where a plain-clone fixture could not expose a per-worktree defect. It also creates NO new entry in the shared gitdir, unlike `git worktree add`, so it is strictly less invasive than the thing it predicts. streams.the_threshold_is_a_protocol_floor_not_a_: His structural point, accepted: a stage whose POINT is to measure a duration must not take its window threshold from a prediction, or the prediction starts guarding the measurement meant to replace it. So 120 s here is not an expected duration - it is sized by the COST OF ERROR, which is unusually symmetric and small in both directions. Starting too late costs a lease in DRAIN_REQUIRED plus a re-run: the action is local, reversible, safely interruptible, creates no entry in the shared gitdir and leaves no /tmp record, so an overrun damages nothing. Refusing too early costs one round. With both costs cheap, the floor is set where a run of the only magnitudes anyone has recorded would finish, while admitting those magnitudes are about other routes. And the floor cannot bias the result: the wall clock is recorded whatever it turns out to be, including if it exceeds the floor. Contrast stage 8, where the cost of error is one-directional - the push cannot be taken back - and 180 s is justified from above.

The pin turns a shift into a REFUSAL BEFORE the action instead of a redness AFTER it. THE PRECISE DESCRIPTION, which is the coordinator's correction to his own first wording and sharper than mine: this is not 'an artefact outside any repository'. It is an artefact with a VERSIONED SOURCE and an UNRECORDED DELIVERY. NARROWING THE BLAST RADIUS, because the narrower statement is the more useful one. He named four asserts (116, 117, 135, 136). streams.four_limits_of_his_that_I_am_carrying_no: (1) `run_harness_commands` calls `subprocess.run(..., shell=True, cwd=repo, capture_output=True)` with NO timeout, so this stage's duration has no upper bound IN THE CODE - a hung harness hangs it, the window expires with a live process, and the resolution is the drain path. This is also the deeper reason a predicted threshold was never the right instrument here: the quantity has no ceiling to predict. (2) `capture_output` holds the output of all nineteen in memory while only an 8-line tail reaches `summary`; this machine killed four processes under memory pressure today, so the risk is not zero and is named. (4) The canonical-checkout control is a COUNT at `--untracked-files=no`, so it is blind to a substitution (one file reverted while another is changed leaves the count equal) and to a new untracked file there. It is a secondary control and its blind spot belongs next to it.
